name: a line opens the block past its indentation and its containers' markers
why: A typed block opens within three columns of the containers a line continues: a quote's `>`, a list item's marker (`-`, `*`, `+`, or digits and `.` or `)`) and a footnote label.

name: a line opens no ask block past what is not a container marker
why: A list marker with no space or tab after it, a blank footnote label, text before the directive, two colons and another block type open no ask block.

name: no line of fenced code opens a block
why: A fence of backticks or tildes, three or more, is closed only by a fence of the same character at least as long with nothing after it but blanks.

name: a line that only starts like a fence opens none
why: A backtick fence's info string holds no backtick, so a line that starts with a code span opens no fence; nor do two backticks.

name: a fence opened past a container's marker is code like any other
why: A fence opened in a quote, a footnote definition or a list item ends with that container, and what it holds is code.

name: no line of the front matter a document opens with opens a block
why: pmdoc keeps front matter as one node, word for word: a `---` and any spaces or tabs opens it and the first later line that is the same closes it.

name: front matter opens only on the first line
why: A rule after text is no front matter.

name: an opening `---` nothing closes is no front matter
why: An opening `---` that nothing closes is no front matter, and after it no typed block opens at the document's level (pmdoc's frontmatterAttempt, which wraps the typed block's parser in pmdoc/parse.go). The opener is paragraph text.

name: after an opening `---` nothing closes, neither a callout nor an ask block in it opens
why: After an opening `---` that nothing closes, a callout does not open at the document's level either, so the ask block's opener inside it is paragraph text (pmdoc's frontmatterAttempt).

name: a footnote label holds an escaped bracket, and a block opens on its line
why: A backslash before ASCII punctuation escapes it, so `\]` and `\[` are part of the label. An unescaped `[` makes the line no footnote label.

name: a fence opened on the line of a footnote label that holds an escaped bracket is code
why: The fence a label's line opens holds the lines of the definition that follow it, four columns in.

name: a line of an inline code span four columns past its containers opens no block
why: An inline code span keeps the spaces at the start of its later lines, so such a line can start with an opener. Four columns or more past its containers' lines, the line goes on with the paragraph and opens no block. The columns of a footnote definition or a list item that the line goes on with are its containers' columns.

name: a line four columns past its containers' markers opens no block
why: An opener four columns or more past the marker before it is indented code.

name: a list stays open at a line that reaches its empty last item's content column
why: An empty item takes its content from the next line where that line reaches the item's content column and no blank line stands between them. So the list stays open, though goldmark closes it at a marker of another bullet character (pmdoc's emptyItemGuard.Continue).

name: after indented code, an item numbered 10 opens a list in the quote a line of `>` opened
why: After indented code, a line of only `>` counts as blank only where the list opens in no container that its own line opens (pmdoc's interruptsOpenBlock). Here the `>` line opened the quote a line before the item, so the code holds nothing open on the item's line, and the item numbered 10 opens a list in the quote.

name: a block opened on the line of a footnote label that holds an escaped bracket
why: A backslash in a footnote's label escapes the `]` after it, as the renderer writes a label that holds one (pmdoc's escapeFootnoteLabel), so a block written on that label's line opens there.

name: a fence opened on the line of a footnote label that holds an escaped bracket, then a block after it
why: A fence written on that label's line opens there, so the opener inside it is code.

name: a later block of a footnote four columns in, after a fence the label's line opened
why: The definition's later blocks stand four columns in, as the renderer writes them.

name: a later block of a footnote four columns in
why: A footnote definition's later blocks stand four columns in, as the renderer writes them.

name: a block opened on the line of a footnote label that holds only a form feed
why: A label of a form feed is a label: goldmark's white space is the space, the tab and the line endings alone.

name: a line of indented code
why: A line four columns or more past its containers opens no block: it is indented code.

name: a line four columns past a quote's marker or a list item's
why: The columns after a quote's `>` and a list item's marker are its containers' columns, so a line four past them is indented code.

name: a line after a front-matter opener that no line closes
why: After a front-matter opener that no line closes, no typed block opens at the document's level (pmdoc's frontmatterAttempt).
